Phenotype name: severe developmental delay and/or mental retardation
AS specific behaviour typified by an easily excitable personality with an inappropriately happy affect
two or more tumors eventually developed in 20 of the patients
intracranial nontumoral calcifications were present in most patients
the presence of such lesions is probably a prodromic feature of neurofibromatosis 2
meningiomas and ependymomas were more common among the young patients
posterior subcapsular or capsular, cortical, or mixed lens opacities
partial seizures with eye deviation and vomiting
All patients were ataxic, severely retarded, and lacking recognisable speech
Hypotonia at birth was recorded in 15/24 (63%) and neonatal feeding difficulties were recorded in 20/26 (77%)
Epilepsy was present in 26/27 (96%) with onset by the third year of life in 20 patients (83%)
An abnormal EEG was reported in 25/25 patients
Five patients could not walk independently
Disrupted sleep patterns were present in 18/21 patients (86%), with improvement in 9/12 patients (75%) over 10 years of age
All nine who walked were ataxic with an awkward, clumsy, heavy, and/or lilting gait
